title: [CQ-C02b] Snapshot manifest source adapter
description:
Objective: Let the C02 bounded repository source provider (packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.ts) also serve from R09's validated source snapshot manifests (protected base plus actual overlay bytes), so an isolated session's context matches the snapshot it was given.

Context: This is the dependent remainder of the original C02. On 2026-10-25 the operator re-sliced C02 to run now over immutable Git commit ids only; it reports uncommitted/overlay bytes as the explicit limitation 'committed-bytes-only'. This row carries C02's former dependencies: R09 (manifest format) and C01 (packet vocabulary, which adopts C02's types). Consume the LANDED R09 manifest format, C02 provider and C01 packet. Do not invent or redefine any of them, and keep C02's refusal and explicit-status semantics unchanged.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: A query against an R09-validated snapshot manifest serves base and overlay bytes with per-item provenance naming the manifest identity and the content hash derived from the served bytes, not from writer declarations.
Overlay paths that traverse outside the root, symlink escapes and .git/.moe/control paths are refused, consistent with R09's import validation and C02's refusal codes.
Missing, stale or unverifiable overlay entries remain explicit and never silently fall back to base, working-tree or other unvalidated bytes.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Reuse C02's total-byte cap rather than copying it. In packages/moe-daemon/src/context/repositorySource.ts:
- Export capTotal as a generic, `export function capTotal<T extends SourceItem>(items: T[], maxBytes: number): T[]`, with a narrow `as T` on the omitted object if TypeScript needs it.
- Make NO behavior change: same order, same 'omitted'/'total-byte-cap' rewrite, content and matches stripped, bytes 0.
- Nothing else in the file changes. C02's refusal and explicit-status semantics stay untouched (task description), and the CQ-C02 size rail is about C02's own landed bytes.
Confirm src/context/repositorySource.test.ts and repositorySource.service.test.ts still pass unchanged in the Linux-native snapshot (mem gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate: whole-repo git archive HEAD, overlay only this task's files, symlinked native node_modules, env -i with the nvm node bin on PATH, NO_COLOR=1).

Implement the adapter in a new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/snapshotSource.ts. It is PURE and SYNCHRONOUS: it imports only from './repositorySource.js' and './snapshotManifest.js' (C02b1), plus Buffer and performance. No fs, child_process, cachedPlanPaths or Git.

API:
- `export interface SnapshotProvenance { readonly layer: 'base' | 'overlay'; readonly manifest: string; readonly sha256: string }`. manifest is the recomputed digest of the layer that supplied the bytes. sha256 is the verified entry's hash, recomputed by C02b1 from the same private copy that is served: derived from the served bytes, never from a writer declaration.
- `export interface SnapshotSourceMatch extends SourceMatch { provenance: SnapshotProvenance }`.
- `export interface SnapshotSourceItem extends Omit<SourceItem, 'oid' | 'matches'> { provenance?: SnapshotProvenance; matches?: SnapshotSourceMatch[] }`.
- `export interface SnapshotSource { manifest: { commit: string; tree: string | null; base: string | null; overlay: string | null }; items: SnapshotSourceItem[]; complete: boolean; limitations: string[]; bytes: number }`.
- `export interface SnapshotRequest { commit: string; base?: string; overlay?: string }`.
- `export function readSnapshotSource(snapshot: unknown, request: SnapshotRequest, queries: SourceQuery[], options: { limits?: Partial<SourceLimits> } = {}): SnapshotSource`.

Order of operations:
1. Caller errors throw first, as in C02. Run validateSourceRequest(request.commit, queries, options.limits). That refuses '..' traversal, absolute and backslash paths and bad ids with INVALID_INPUT. request.base and request.overlay, when given, must be 64-char lowercase hex, else invalidInput. Copy the queries.
2. verifySourceSnapshot(snapshot). If it is not ok, EVERY item becomes 'unavailable' with reason `snapshot-unverifiable:<code>`. The manifest is {commit: request.commit, tree: null, base: null, overlay: null}, and limitations include 'snapshot-unverifiable'.
3. Stale check. If snapshot.commit !== request.commit, or request.base / request.overlay differs from the recomputed identity, EVERY item becomes 'unavailable' with reason 'snapshot-stale'. The manifest reports the recomputed identity actually received, and limitations include 'snapshot-stale'.
- There is never a fallback to base, worktree or other bytes.

Read query (path P):
1. snapshotPathRefusal(P): SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_PATH gives 'refused'/'control-path'; SNAPSHOT_PATH_INVALID gives 'refused'/'path-invalid'.
2. A proper ancestor of P that is a file in the merged view gives 'missing'/'not-in-manifest'.
3. An overlay delete at P gives 'missing'/'deleted-in-overlay'.
4. Otherwise serve: the overlay file, else the base file. If P is a directory prefix of any merged file, give 'refused'/'not-a-file'; if it is absent, 'missing'/'not-in-manifest'.
5. Serving a file: path, mode '100755' or '100644', size and provenance. Bytes containing NUL give 'refused'/'binary' with no content. Decode the first maxFileBytes with a fatal TextDecoder (stream:true when truncated), exactly as C02's readBlob. A decode failure gives 'refused'/'not-utf8'. size > maxFileBytes gives 'truncated'/'file-byte-cap'. bytes = Buffer.byteLength(content).

Search query (literal L, optional scopes):
- Each scope goes through snapshotPathRefusal ('control-path' / 'path-invalid' refused). A deleted scope gives 'missing'/'deleted-in-overlay'. An absent scope that is neither a file nor a directory prefix gives 'missing'/'scope-not-in-manifest'. A file or directory scope is fine.
- Scan the merged files (overlay files win, deletes hide base) in UTF-8 path-byte order, filtered by scope (equal, or prefix plus '/'). Split each file's bytes on 0x0a; line numbers start at 1; a final unterminated line counts; a '\r' stays in the text, as git grep -F -n -a prints it. Match with Buffer indexOf on the literal's UTF-8 bytes.
- A matched line containing NUL, or that is not valid UTF-8, is skipped with reason 'undecodable-match'.
- Stop at maxMatches with 'match-cap'. When the next match's Buffer.byteLength(path)+Buffer.byteLength(text) would exceed maxSearchBytes, stop with 'search-byte-cap'.
- The status is 'served' with no reason, else 'truncated' with the first reason. Every match carries its file's provenance. bytes is the sum of path+text bytes, as in C02. Push the 'literal-search-only' limitation.

Budget:
- One deadline for the whole call: performance.now() + limits.timeBudgetMs, checked between files.
- A search cut off by the deadline is 'truncated'/'time-budget' with its partial matches. Every later query is 'unavailable'/'time-budget'.
- This bounds the synchronous CPU, because a snapshot may hold 256 MiB.

Result:
- Apply capTotal(items, maxTotalBytes).
- complete = every item 'served'.
- limitations: sorted and unique, always including 'snapshot-bytes'.
- manifest {commit, tree, base: identity.base, overlay: identity.overlay}.

Each call verifies once; callers batch up to maxQueries queries per call. Error handling: the verifier never throws, and hostile snapshot input only yields statuses; only caller-shape errors throw.

Write the unit tests in a new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/snapshotSource.test.ts. Keep them table-driven to stay inside the 400 net-line budget, tests included.

Fixtures:
- Build raw SourceSnapshots through the LANDED producer: `await import(pathToFileURL(<repo>/scripts/local-runner/source-snapshot.mjs).href)` validateImport, assembled as {version:1, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded:0}.
- Resolve the repo root relatively from import.meta.url. Use describe.skipIf on the file's absence for the Docker context.
- Base: 'src/a.ts', 'src/b.ts', 'docs/x.md', a NUL-bearing 'bin.dat', a non-UTF-8 'latin1.txt', and a 70-byte 'big.txt' with a multibyte char at the cap boundary.
- Overlay: modify 'src/a.ts', add 'src/new.ts', and delete 'docs/x.md'.

Cases. Assert exact status, reason, content and bytes, and check provenance with a sha256 the TEST computes over the bytes:
- S1: base-only read is served with layer 'base', manifest equal to the overlay-independent base digest, mode and size.
- S2: overlay-modified read serves the overlay bytes (layer 'overlay', sha256 differs from base).
- S3: overlay-added read.
- S4: overlay-deleted read gives 'missing'/'deleted-in-overlay', with content undefined and bytes 0. That proves there is no base fallback.
- S5: control paths '.moe/project.json', '.GIT/config' and 'src/.git/x' are 'refused'/'control-path'.
- S6: paths valid for C02 but invalid for R09 ('CON.txt', 'a/PROGRA~1/x', and NFD 'é.ts') are 'refused'/'path-invalid'.
- S7: '../x' and 'a/../b' throw INVALID_INPUT naming queries[i].path before any verification. A spy/flag fixture is not needed: assert the throw.
- S8: the directory 'src' gives 'not-a-file', 'src/a.ts/child' gives 'not-in-manifest', and an absent path gives 'not-in-manifest'.
- S9: 'bin.dat' gives 'binary' and 'latin1.txt' gives 'not-utf8', both with no content. With limits {maxFileBytes: 64}, 'big.txt' gives 'truncated'/'file-byte-cap' with exactly the decodable prefix.
- S10: unverifiable inputs are each mutated from a good fixture after freezing: a copied entry with a wrong sha256, a wrong layer digest, an overlay entry at '.moe/x', and a {kind:'symlink'} entry. EVERY item, including the base-only path, is 'unavailable' with reason 'snapshot-unverifiable:<CODE>' and no content, limitations include 'snapshot-unverifiable', and complete is false.
- S11: a request commit mismatch, a request.base mismatch and a request.overlay mismatch each give all items 'unavailable'/'snapshot-stale'. A bad request.base shape throws INVALID_INPUT.
- S12: a search finds the literal in base-only 'src/b.ts' and overlay-modified 'src/a.ts', sorted by path then line, each with its provenance. A literal present ONLY in the base bytes of the modified 'src/a.ts', or only in deleted 'docs/x.md', is NOT matched.
- S13: scope 'src' limits matches. Scope '.moe' is 'refused'/'control-path', scope 'docs/x.md' is 'missing'/'deleted-in-overlay', and scope 'nope' is 'missing'/'scope-not-in-manifest'.
- S14: maxMatches 1 gives 'match-cap' with exactly one match. A tiny maxSearchBytes gives 'search-byte-cap'. A matched line with NUL or invalid UTF-8 gives 'undecodable-match' and is not returned. A CRLF line keeps its '\r'.
- S15: a small maxTotalBytes makes later items 'omitted'/'total-byte-cap' with content stripped.
- S16: timeBudgetMs 1 over a large multi-file snapshot gives 'time-budget' (truncated, then unavailable), and nothing throws.
- S17: the module source imports no 'node:fs', 'fs', 'child_process' or 'cachedPlanPaths'. Read it as text; this is a static purity check. The input queries array and snapshot are not mutated.

Mutation proof, on a scratch copy of the snapshot only:
- remove the overlay-delete branch: S4 red;
- drop the stale check: S11 red;
- serve base when the overlay is unverifiable: S10 red;
- swap the scope filter: S13 red;
- remove the NUL guard: S9/S14 red.
Record the results in the step note.

Add an end-to-end conformance test against the real producer and C02, in the same test file. It is skipped only when scripts/ is absent.
1. In a mkdtemp git repo (follow repositorySource.test.ts's temp-repo helper pattern: execFileSync git with a scrubbed env, cleaned in afterAll), commit 'keep.ts', 'edit.ts' and 'gone.ts'. Then modify 'edit.ts' and delete 'gone.ts' in the worktree, add an untracked 'add.ts', and add an untracked '.moe/state.json'.
2. Run the LANDED scripts/local-runner/source-export.mjs exportSourceSnapshot({repoDir, commit}).
3. Assert through readSnapshotSource:
- 'keep.ts' content and status equal what readRepositorySource(root, commit, same query) serves. This is C02 parity for committed bytes.
- 'edit.ts' serves the dirty bytes from the overlay.
- 'gone.ts' is 'missing'/'deleted-in-overlay'.
- 'add.ts' is served from the overlay.
- '.moe/state.json' is 'refused'/'control-path'. R09b excluded it, and the adapter refuses rather than reports it missing.
- The result manifest's base and overlay equal the export's base.digest and overlay.digest.
Error handling: if the export throws, fail the test with its code. Never skip on an export failure.

Verification, once, fresh. In a Linux-native snapshot (whole-repo git archive HEAD, overlay ONLY this task's three files plus the landed C02b1 module if it is not yet in HEAD, symlinked native node_modules, env -i):

- `npx tsc --noEmit` must exit 0.

Adversarial self-review: load adversarial-self-review and walk this task's own diff. This is the last step.
- Can ANY path through readSnapshotSource serve bytes that verification did not cover, or fall back to base after an overlay delete, a refusal, staleness or unverifiability?
- Can a hostile snapshot make it throw, loop unboundedly or block past timeBudgetMs?
- Is provenance ever taken from a writer declaration instead of the verified copy?
- Are C02's statuses and reasons reused verbatim where they apply ('not-in-manifest', 'not-a-file', 'binary', 'not-utf8', 'file-byte-cap', 'match-cap', 'search-byte-cap', 'undecodable-match', 'total-byte-cap'), with the new reasons limited to: 'control-path', 'path-invalid', 'deleted-in-overlay', 'snapshot-unverifiable:<code>', 'snapshot-stale', 'time-budget'?
- Does any project global forbiddenPattern token appear in the code or tests?
Report every path in complete_step.modifiedFiles: repositorySource.ts, snapshotSource.ts and snapshotSource.test.ts. Write the task handoff memory with the final interface for C04 and C05.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. One task for verification plus serving: about 420 lines with tests, over QA's 400 net cap. Split: the pure verifier became CQ-C02b1 (task-02fd5931, created 2026-10-29 with the exact interface in its description). This row serves read and search over the verified view.
2. Make the adapter read the worktree or Git for overlay paths. Rejected by the DoD: only R09-validated manifest bytes may be served, with no working-tree fallback.
3. Accept only a pre-verified view. Rejected: DoD3 needs unverifiable input to surface as explicit statuses, so the adapter takes the raw snapshot and verifies it once per call. Callers batch queries; there is no cache (YAGNI until activation).
4. Extend C02's RepositorySource/SourceItem types. Rejected, because they are a shared contract the C01 packet adopts. The new Snapshot* types extend them in the new module, and C02's file gains only one export.
5. Treat '.moe/...' queries as 'missing'. Rejected: R09b excludes control paths, so 'refused'/'control-path' keeps the reason explicit and consistent with R09a's SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_PATH.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Landed facts this plan relies on:
- C02 readRepositorySource is git-only, committed bytes, statuses served|truncated|omitted|missing|refused|unavailable.
- validateSourceRequest is exported and pure.
- capTotal is private; step 1 exports it.
- C02's normalizedPath already refuses '..', absolute paths and backslashes, but admits control and R09-unportable paths (CON.txt, 8.3 names, NFD). The adapter refuses those through snapshotPathRefusal.
- R09b exportSourceSnapshot resolves a frozen {version:1, commit, tree, base, overlay, excluded}.
  - base and overlay are validateImport results {entries sorted by UTF-8 path bytes, digest}.
  - A file entry is {kind, path, executable, size, sha256, data}; a delete is {kind, path}.
  - Control paths are excluded and counted.
- R09a's digest framing is 'moe-source-snapshot-v1\\0', u32be count, then per entry a kind byte, path, and for a file the exec byte, size and raw sha256.
- The daemon cannot import scripts/*.mjs at runtime (separate package). Tests may import them by repo-relative URL, skipped when scripts/ is absent (the Docker context).

Assumed, unlanded interface: C02b1 snapshotManifest.ts, exactly as named in task-02fd5931's description:
- verifySourceSnapshot returning {ok:true, snapshot} | {ok:false, code, layer?};
- VerifiedSnapshot {commit, tree, identity{base, overlay}, base Map, overlay Map with delete markers, excluded};
- snapshotPathRefusal.
planningNotes.risks:
- Synchronous CPU over up to 256 MiB: the deadline keeps it bounded, and S16 pins it.
- Explicitness: every no-serve path must stay explicit (S4, S10, S11). A single base fallback is the critical defect class.
- Search semantics mirror git grep -F -n -a closely but not byte for byte: C02 caps the raw git output, while this caps path+text bytes. Document the difference in a code comment and pin it with S14.
- WSL: the daemon tests run only in a Linux-native snapshot.
- Dependencies:
  - C02b1 must land first; it is in dependsOn.
  - R09 final (task-0dd1cce2, REVIEW) is kept per the directive but not consumed: R09b/R09a are the producers.
- Size: 400 net lines including tests, with no exception. Prefer table-driven cases.
- Rails: no forbidden tokens, no .moe edits, no Git writes. Test repos live in temp dirs only.
